We're currently speccing out first-class i18n behavior for Next.js, so this PR will probably be delayed until after that RFC is implemented since these two PRs overlap in scope:
https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/17078

Please add any feedback you may have on that RFC!

body: Amazing Work! but how do we generate static pages using getStaticProps?? Since JAMStack is biggest advantage of NEXT.js!
author: raghav0622

body: @raghav0622 In this example the data is behind user authentication, you can't pregenerate the content in that case, so it uses client side rendering instead, all the content is still static but the data is fetched in the client. If the data didn't depend on the user then you can go for `getStaticProps` 👍
author: lfades

body:
> @raghav0622 In this example the data is behind user authentication, you can't pregenerate the content in that case, so it uses client side rendering instead, all the content is still static but the data is fetched in the client. If the data didn't depend on the user then you can go for `getStaticProps` 👍

just a scenario where on build time all public data like blog posts or in this case movie titles can be fetched on build time in getStaticProps with anonymous authentication provided by realm-web (there is nodejs sdk just like firebase-admin), editing/upading relvanat data / blog posts is user-auth dependent

body:
> The common way of redirecting is fine, we don't have to match Express helpers. If redirecting is complicated then maybe we can mention it on docs instead and/or create an example for it.

Because so many people use Express and expect this helper (I myself was confused why it didn't exist) it would be wise to add it. It also solves a lot of problems with other libraries such as Passport.js, where certain auth strategy middlewares use the `res.redirect` helper internally.

body: @christianalfoni Sorry, left some comments a bit late. I've been working on a demo to showcase Stitches SSR and CRP and have been referring to this. After a while of having some unexpected rendering issues, I decided to clone this and test here as well. At first it worked fine, until I realised this project and mine had different versions of Next.js. This uses Next v9.3.5 and I was using v9.4.4. Changing this to use Next v9.4 surfaces the same issues I'm having, which is: - Make a change - HMR kicks in and applies new styles - Refresh browser twice - Styles are gone ![stitches-next](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/372831/86741462-b0ca3e80-c037-11ea-8ca2-d364a57e0edb.gif) ![CleanShot 2020-07-07 at 09 53 09@2x](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/372831/86741452-adcf4e00-c037-11ea-9a98-49dcd697be28.png) --- Also: it looks like the css vars and being defined twice, had you noticed that too?

body:
> @iamsharzil  Hi there thank you for the PR and sorry for the late review!
> 
> I have never used Magento before and the readme assumes that I have a Magento account (which I don't), can you share a live demo of the example that I can review? 
> 
> If hosting Magento is not free (I did a small research and looks like there aren't good free options) then I would like to review a demo before digging more deep into the example.

@lfades Hi Luis, Can you please tell me how and what would you like to see in the live demo? 
I created this example with the staging environment of my client's account. But if you would want I can share a video explaining the Magento side steps. Please let me know I'm happy to share it with you.
author: iamsharzil

body: @iamsharzil We don't have any other e-commerce examples with the exception of this open PR for a shopify example: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/15137 - It has a demo available (https://nextjs-shopify.vercel.app/) - I would like to see something like that or better. Ideally I would like to see something that would make me want to use Magento, but that starts with a live demo I can review 🙏

body: 🤔  This is causing redirect loops on the `trailing-slashes` integration tests
author: Janpot

body:
We might need to keep this strict. We were making this change to fix a bug in `path-to-regexp`:

**Correct**
```
> require('path-to-regexp').pathToRegexp('/:stuff*', [], {strict:true}).test('/ab')
true

> require('path-to-regexp').pathToRegexp('/:stuff*', [], {strict:true}).test('/ab/')
false

> require('path-to-regexp').pathToRegexp('/:stuff*', [], {strict:false}).test('/')
true

> require('path-to-regexp').pathToRegexp('/:stuff*', [], {strict:true}).test('')
true
```

**Incorrect**
```
> require('path-to-regexp').pathToRegexp('/:stuff*', [], {strict:true}).test('/')
false
```

---

Let's fix the bug in `path-to-regexp` instead?
author: Timer

body: Opened issue here https://github.com/pillarjs/path-to-regexp/issues/228
author: Timer

body: They confirmed the behavior is intentional in case users are passing non-prefixed paths.
author: Timer

body: Closing this PR since the behavior is currently intentional, we misunderstood how it should work.

body:
@isaachinman Wouldn't using namespaces solve that?

Anyway, here's my use case for context:
1. I didn't want to bundle my translations in the `public/` folder and send the entire translation json files to the client's browser.
2. I didn't want any language specifc routes in my application like `/en` or `/de`.
3. I wanted to use hooks for translations since they're straightforward and don't require me to add any additional components in my code. That's the primary reason I avoided `react-intl`.
4. I had no use for an i18n backend or language detector. Setting the default language in i18n config works fine.

It took me several days to figure out `react-i18next` can even work with `Next.js` without setting up Express or using something like `rosetta` or `redirects()`. This example would've made life much easier if it was present in Next.js repo before I started so I decided to make a minimal example and send a PR.

Please let me know if this adds any caveats that I need to mention in the readme. But for my particular use case, this is the exact example I was looking for. Just straightforward translations with `react-i18next`, nothing else needed.

author: isaachinman

body:
@isaachinman That sounds awesome! I've been waiting for `rewrites()` to be released as stable for some time now so we can use it in production and stop depending on Express to do API routing. ( Related: #14634 )

Regarding `react-i18next`, I believe there should be an example available on how to use it directly. `Next.js` is awesome, but people using it are still React developers and search for "How to do this with React" first before searching "How to do this with Next.js".

This was the case with me. Searched for translations with React, found `react-i18next`, added the code to my `Next.js` project, and after hours realized that their official example doesn't work with `Next.js`. Almost migrated my entire project to Razzle in frustration before realizing there was this workaround.

Regarding `next-i18next`, perhaps the serverless example reference can be added to the `Next.js` or `react-i18next` tutorial or docs so it's easier to stumble into?

body:
@cseas The example you've submitted with this PR is not something which people should take guidance from, in my opinion. It _works_, yes, but there are many antipatterns that will cause serious issues for projects of any reasonable size. As you have found out, it is indeed possible to use `react-i18next` directly with NextJs and make things _work_, but once you look into it any deeper than surface level, you will realise that it's actually a semi-complex problem to solve. That's why `next-i18next` and various other packages exist.

Just one example – in your example app here, an English user would end up downloading all German translations, despite never needing them. In fact, it looks like every user would download every language, and every namespace.
author: isaachinman

body:
@isaachinman Ah, got it. Would that be because of using the `resources` instead of a `Backend` in `i18n` `init()` and just the way `i18n` works? Or is this specific to `Next.js` and using `resources` is fine otherwise?

I didn't really understand what benefits the http backend gives to i18n over just importing the json files. Is there any documentation available that would cover this explanation?
author: cseas

body:
Correct. The docs are on the [repo](https://github.com/i18next/i18next-http-backend).

We need some kind of resource backend to fetch assets per language and per namespace, as needed. In a NextJs context, we may introduce new language or namespace requirements on the client side after a new component mounts, or the route changes. You can see logic to cover the route change case in `next-i18next` [here](https://github.com/isaachinman/next-i18next/blob/master/src/hocs/app-with-translation.tsx#L57), for example.

To summarise my view on i18n in NextJs: unless you are a large org that has the desire and capacity to roll your own solution, you should probably just grab an off-the-shelf solution, as it will save you a lot of time and headache in the long run. I think that promoting these "simple i18n" examples is actually a disservice to new devs, and I have seen this same pattern play out countless times in the past couple years.
author: isaachinman

body: @cseas Okay with closing the PR based on @isaachinman comments? I agree with him and the current state of the example is not ideal. `rewrites` are going to be released in the next stable release as everything for them is ready, including the docs.
author: lfades

body:
@lfades Yeah that sounds alright. I still wish `Next.js` supported other libraries that React projects usually do though. This is just a beginner's perspective but coming from `create-react-app` or a custom `webpack` toolchain, it really feels like a paradigm shift trying to switch to `Next.js` to get server-side rendering. React router doesn't work, react-i18next is discouraged, and idk how many more of these replacements do I have to learn for a switch.

I like the features of Next and wish I could promote it where I work. But the concept of "use only Next libraries for everything" feels too restrictive as a developer. I might give Razzle a try, still exploring options for a new project.

author: ijjk

body:
Been doing a some digging today and the test issue has already occurred [once before](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/12952) it seems, where the result has been that @StarpTech has submitted a [pull request](https://github.com/michael-ciniawsky/postcss-load-plugins/pull/119) to [postcss-load-plugins](https://github.com/michael-ciniawsky/postcss-load-plugins), which now has been two months stale. The proposed changes would hopefully result in code that is easier to follow, but I still think that it would requires some change in [styled-jsx-plugin-postcss](https://github.com/giuseppeg/styled-jsx-plugin-postcss) to get it working all the way through. 

I am still uncertain of why the bug happens in the first place. I tried running the styledstyled-jsx-plugin-postcss through the next babel preset with the different versions of babel and they both came out identical from what I could see.

If anyone has some pointers on where to look next (pun-intended) I'll see if I can find the time :)
author: Bjodol

body:
Hi @Bjodol are you still working on this PR? There are some conflicts but next@canary hasn't updated yet to babel 7.10. You can run the styled-jsx tests locally and see why they broke:

```bash
yarn testonly --testPathPattern=integration/styled-jsx-plugin
```

See [contributing.md](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/contributing.md) for more detailed steps.

body:
@lfades do you mean the posts inside the posts folder, like `blog-starter-mdx/pages/posts/foo-bar.mdx`? I tried this approach (it is actually what I am doing now with my blog) and I didn't like it so far for these reasons:
1. the posts are all inside the `pages/posts` folder, imo it is more organized at the top level like in the `blog-starter` example
2. all the posts have the same layout boilerplate (import and exporting the component), I don't mind it too much but it is still a negative point
3. all pages have the "layout code" inside `pages/`, but the posts are the only exception where the layout has to be outside the pages folder 

The downside of the solution of this PR is the little fact that HMR doesn't work at all, lol

Both solutions are able to use all the advantages of MDX, with exception of imports inside the MDX source that isn't a big deal since you can still inject the custom components like I did with the `Counter` in this example. So both solutions have trade-offs

With all that said, I am happy to change to the pages approach if you think it is better as an example, we can still document the `next-mdx-remote` approach in the README

body: @rafaelalmeidatk I'm okay with this PR and I don't see any issues with it, it just feels incredible similar to the md blog, with the difference that it adds a counter 🤔. I don't see how is MDX being really different here, but that may be just me 🤷‍♂️

body: Next.js does not know about a custom server existing as the server calls Next.js so Next.js can't do hot module replacement of custom server code hence why nodemon is needed there. However nodemon is configured incorrectly in the example, it should only watch for changes in the server file, not any other files
author: timneutkens

body:
@lfades I have a question and can't seem to find an answer.

When you build this example, you **don't get a separate `chunk` for the library**, instead it's bundled inside each page.
The **same applies for** the examples for [Fela](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-fela) and **Compiled**.

However, for other **CSS-in-JS** solutions like [Styled Components](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-styled-components), [Emotion](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-emotion), [Stitches](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-stitches), [JSS](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-react-jss) or [TypeStyle](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-typestyle) you **get a separate `chunk` of the lib**, that is shared across all pages.

So, the questions are:
- why is this difference? is there a reason for getting handled differently?
- is there a way to control what gets to common chunks, and what not? (I've searched all the docs, without any luck)

I would really appreciate if you could shed some light.

I'm working on a [thorough analysis of all CSS-in-JS](https://github.com/andreipfeiffer/css-in-js) solutions with Next.js, and can't get my head around this tiny bit.

body: When you navigate from a product page and the homepage the cart data doesn't persist and is cleared.
author: richyrb00

body: @richyrb00 There's currently no cache for the cart, looks like I should be using `localStorage` although I wasn't sure of that (there is no API alternative because you can't query an anonymous cart).
author: lfades

body: might be worth looking at https://github.com/Shopify/storefront-api-examples/issues/30#issuecomment-596241212
author: richyrb00

body: infact everything you need should already be there if you import and move <CartProvider> to wrap the <Component> in _app.js it now works when moving from different page templates. the only add on you might want to do is if the user navigates away from the site and comes back you would want to maintain the cart data and so storing it in local storage and then if it exists pulling the data down would be the ideal.
author: richyrb00

body: Closing for now, in the future we'll have https://github.com/vercel/commerce updated to be integrated with Shopify instead of having an example here. Also I no longer have a free account in Shopify that I can use to run this example.

body:
As per the [migration guide](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/react/migrating/apollo-client-3-migration/#graphql-tag) I think you could also remove `graphql-tag` as a dependency and import it from `@apollo/client` as well! :)

Just a guess, but [same](https://www.apollographql.com/docs/react/migrating/apollo-client-3-migration/#apolloreact-hoc-and-apolloreact-components) for `graphql` as well. And cannot `ApolloClient` also be directly imported from `@apollo/client` instead of `@apollo/client/core`? That one might just be a personal preference, so leave it if you disagree, but maybe it could mirror better how in v3 you only need one import to achieve anything.
author: balazsorban44

body:
I could, but `gql` from `graphql-tag` is 35.8kb and the `gql` from `@apollo/client` is 107.4kb.
I tried to build, seems ~1kb difference with my project, so i changed the import and removed `graphql-tag`.

Tried to import `ApolloClient` from `@apollo/client` and it works, that's nice.
Can't remove `graphql` though, it is needed.

body:
Hi @lfades! Unless I'm missing something, I don't think the existing example works for apps that need SSR. I discuss this in the README in this PR. The challenge is that the Firebase access token expires after 1 hour, so the user's token won't be accessible server-side for returning users unless it's refreshed server-side, which this example handles.

I agree that the other example is best for any apps that are okay with providing a static initial page then fetching data after the Firebase JS SDK initializes.
author: kmjennison

body:
@kmjennison 

> I don't think the existing example works for apps that need SSR. I discuss this in the README in this PR. The challenge is that the Firebase access token expires after 1 hour, so the user's token won't be accessible server-side for returning users unless it's refreshed server-side, which this example handles.

That seems to be an app config not related to SSR (and I think that default is okay in an example): 

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/bdc465092b0bcfad53b7fecc8f1c0a33bb7e778e/examples/with-firebase-authentication/utils/auth/userCookies.js#L15

And because it's a cookie, it should be accessible by SSR too.

If the current example is missing some updates to make it work for both SSR and static, then let's update it instead 🙏  - Next.js is hybrid and you shouldn't be forced to decide one pre-rendering process over the other. Cookies should work in both cases.
author: lfades

body:
@lfades Sure, it makes sense to merge this functionality into the existing Firebase example. I'll update the issue description to reflect this. (The primary reason for this example to be separate is that the token refresh logic is unnecessarily complicated if a developer knows they'll never need SSR.)

Regarding the expiring cookie you reference above: the limitation is that the server side won't have access to the user when they revisit the site an hour after their last visit, given the cookie has expired and there isn't a refresh token.
author: kmjennison

body:
> Regarding the expiring cookie you reference above: the limitation is that the server side won't have access to the user when they revisit the site an hour after their last visit, given the cookie has expired and there isn't a refresh token.

@kmjennison That's okay. Feel free to remove the expiration date then so the cookie never expires. A refresh token can make the example way more complicated
author: lfades

body: @lfades If we remove the cookie expiration, the server side will have the Firebase user info but won't have a working Firebase ID token. The ID token is necessary to access Firebase services or other services that require the token for authorization.
author: kmjennison

body: @kmjennison I see. Feel free to fix it in the best way possible. I'm not a Firebase expert but I'll be happy to investigate more once you have a PR with the changes 👍
author: lfades

body: @lfades Sounds good 👍 This PR already has working code, so the only thing to do is merge it with the existing example.
author: kmjennison

body:
@kmjennison I recommend refactoring to this approach: https://vriad.com/essays/nextjs-firebase-authentication. TLDR: use the `onIdTokenChanged` listener instead of `onAuthStateChanged` and refresh the cookie inside the callback. Solves all the stale cookie problems. At that point it probably makes sense to merge it into the existing Firebase example as well. 

Great work with this by the way.
author: colinhacks

body:
@vriad Thanks, it makes sense to use `onIdTokenChanged` instead of `onAuthStateChanged`. However, because that token refresh only happens on the client side when the app is running, that doesn't guarantee a valid Firebase ID token on the server side. E.g., if a user does not have the client app running for an hour, then requests a page, the server will receive an expired ID token. This example fixes that by handling token refresh on the server side.

The example you shared looks like it would work great if you don't need a valid ID token for SSR, only user identity. Let me know if you think I'm missing something, though!
author: kmjennison

body:
@kmjennison Hm I see where you're coming from. In that scenario I would just redirect the user to a login page so they can re-authenticate and get a new token. I work primarily in the medical domain so I _want_ to force the user to re-authenticate in that scenario. 

I don't understand this distinction:

> it would work great if don't need a valid ID token for SSR, only user identity

Can you elaborate on that?
author: colinhacks

body: @vriad Makes sense. Regarding the ID token, I mean that a cookie containing auth info can be as long-lived as you want if you're not using the ID token server-side. In that case, you can just store user info (like user ID, email, other claims) in the auth cookie and use it for as long as the cookie exists, then update the cookie as needed on the client side. This is what the existing Firebase auth example does in this repo. The approach of needing a refresh token is really only useful for when you need a valid token server-side—for example, to fetch data from a Firebase service or other service that requires the token for authorization.
author: kmjennison

body:
@kmjennison gotcha, thanks.

I suspect doing server-side token refreshes in that scenario is not something most developers would deem worthwhile. To me anyway I’d rather rely on the client side refreshing and ask for reauthorization if it’s been over an hour. Some folks may be misled by this example into thinking the server side toke refresh is required for doing Firebase + SSR
author: colinhacks

body:
@vriad Yes, I agree that most apps are fine to either fetch data on the client side, use SSR without a token, or (like in your case) require sign in again. The README in this PR recommends other approaches for those apps. In my case, however, the app needs SSR for every request, uses tokens to fetch data, and shouldn't frequently sign users out. I think it would be strange if the default SSR behavior in the Next.js example requires developers to choose between having server-side access to the token or frequently signing users out.

The Next.js team would prefer a unified Firebase auth example for all rendering types. The challenge will be to make it clear that some code is optional depending on the app's use case.
author: kmjennison

body: @kmjennison makes sense! thanks for your thoughtful responses. 👍

body:
@lfades I released [next-firebase-auth](https://github.com/gladly-team/next-firebase-auth) to make it easier to use Firebase with Next.js and updated the example to link to it.

The documentation also discusses alternative approaches, such as setting a JavaScript cookie (like the existing Next.js example does), but doesn't provide demos for those. If you prefer, we can link to `next-firebase-auth` and still leave the example here for people who prefer it.
author: kmjennison

body: @lfades Could you please explain exactly what content you'd like to see here? The `next-firebase-auth` ["getting started" documentation](https://github.com/gladly-team/next-firebase-auth#get-started) is detailed, and I don't think it's useful to duplicate it in this README and have to maintain it in two places.
author: kmjennison

body:
> Or provide a title, description and link to the external example.

Basically, because the example is external, only include a single heading and a description with a link.
author: lfades

body: @lfades Ok, reverted the README to a simple title and link, like the [material-ui example](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-material-ui).

Shouldn't it be more advisable to add an Apollo Client v3 example since it is now the latest stable? It would significantly decrease the complexity of imports and the number of dependencies.

Also, there might be easier ways of creating an Apollo Client now, you could maybe check out the [with-apollo](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-apollo) example for inspiration?

body:
> If I understand correctly, this would allow me to specify "module": "commonjs" in my tsconfig.json, so that that after transpilation (such as via ts-node), there will be require expressions instead of import statements. Is that right?

That is correct. Right now, you have to create a separate `tsconfig.xyz.json` that extends your root `tsconfig.json` (you have an example of this below).

> What downstream impact, if any, does this have on Babel & Webpack?

Zero effect. Next.js will always use the correct settings regardless of what you put in `tsconfig.json`.

> Additionally, and this is a known typescript shortcoming microsoft/TypeScript#16640, I'm not sure it helps me much, as I'll still need to use https://www.npmjs.com/package/module-alias to be able to utilize ~/project/relative/paths.

Unfortunately, this is out of scope of Next.js and the rest of your post is correct:
You'll still need to setup bespoke tooling to run arbitrary TypeScript code, as this is a limitation with TypeScript itself.

After this PR lands you'll be able to drop the `tsconfig.script.json` and `project` setting dance though, correct.

---

This PR is a result of what I could derive from our Twitter thread, but I appreciate the additional feedback.
author: Timer

body:
Vercel does offer more tooling that could help in this scenario, however.

If you globally install `@zeit/ncc` (`npm i -g @zeit/ncc`) you should be able to do the following:

```
ncc run scripts/a.ts
```

This would eliminate the need for your `run-script` helper.

--- 

Maybe we could entertain an official command:

```
next run <script>
```

Would you please take the time to open a new feature request?
author: Timer

body: Got it. Thanks.

Is this fixing https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/12046 and https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/11992 as well? Or only preventing the error?

I guess this PR would supercede https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/13456.

On reconsideration of that PR I linked, I suppose we do need to inject asset prefix since it should proxy to the origin.

Can we test the correct URL is being requested somehow (including the asset prefix)?
author: Timer

body:
> Is this fixing #12046 and #11992 as well? Or only preventing the error?

Those seem to be different issues. this PR just fixes the error introduced by the whatwg URL migration (and a few related things I found on the way). But I'll take a look and see if I can incorporate them into this PR as they seem to be closely related.

> Can we test the correct URL is being requested somehow (including the asset prefix)?

In the test suite I wrote it should be possible to record which urls were requested to the proxy and which to the origin

body:
> If we find any more such discrepencies between script type=module browsers

🤔 I'm thinking [`AbortController`](https://caniuse.com/#feat=abortcontroller)?
author: Janpot

body:
@Janpot IMO reservation to introduce any more of these would be based on how many of those browsers would be affected by such a change?
e.g. this affects only Safari 11/12 vs looks like `AbortController` would affect a sizable population of Chrome/Opera along with Safari 11-12. WDYT?
author: prateekbh

body:
> WDYT?

Makes sense, it just came to my mind as it could improve route cancellation logic in the client router
author: Janpot

body: I'm also interested in this. I'd need the `Intl` & `Intl.PluralRules` APIs and some locale data. Ideally it would be possible to configure this?
author: amannn

body: Instead of polyfilling IntersectionObserver, how about making the lazy loading eager in browsers that don't support it? So `Image` would load all `__lazy` images immediately unless the browser supports IntersectionObserver.

body:
Hi and thank you to modify webpack-5 and describe how to do what to get it running fine.
I'm building my SSR web site (server side is Express, client side is React) as it seems to be better than only front side code.
I think this can be add to consideration to do with as an already present reality to practice a web site. And then give a way for dev to get it config easy (i have two config: configClient and configServer object with same option config mode, module and plugins entries, so i expect to add a line to in the clientSide config part only...)

## what i did

1. I did install npm package "crypto-browserify" (started 3 years ago)
1. and try to add something to webpack-5 config to get it running... 
```
    resolve.fallback: { "crypto": require.resolve("crypto-browserify") },
```
as i can read the message tell to do that at webpack run time.
but it failed to recognize this syntax to be valid (so i think the syntax code provide by the warning message is wrong maybe, or not clear enough to indicate where to add this code)

## So, I miss-understand what warning webpack-5 message said it has to be done

warning message said:
```
 If you want to include a polyfill, you need to:
        - add a fallback 'resolve.fallback: { "crypto": require.resolve("crypto-browserify") }'
        - install 'crypto-browserify'
  If you don't want to include a polyfill, you can use an empty module like this:
        resolve.fallback: { "crypto": false }
```

1. where to include the resolve.fallback (and not resolve.alias then) code line ?
2. to clarify 100%, can you write an example of config code ? I think example code is better than sentences to show something about coding.
3. where is the relative documentation page with nice example config to use please ?

## What works and then what i think it should be indicate to be clear
the syntax "resolve.fallback" is wrong. When you indicate resolve.fallback followed by { ... } , it is confused because there is 2 syntax. It can not be clear.
Let's indicate it as simple as it is in JSON object convention like, inside the config webpack file:
```
resolve: { 
    fallback: { 
        "crypto": require.resolve("crypto-browserify")
    }
}
```
to insert inside a config webpack object to assign (the word "assign is important to be clear, because function Object has "assign" method to assign a content to the root Object).
To be clear, we have to employ linked logic words already in use in the syntax. This would be amazingly fantastic for users to directly and clearly understand the messages to reconfigure the Webpack with his new "features" removed.
Thank you so much to consider this as it can be.

So the message warning should be better like this:
```
 If you want to include a polyfill for frontedn/client side, you need to:
        _ install 'crypto-browserify'
        _ assign this new entry to the config file of Webpack-5: 'resolve: fallback: { { "crypto": require.resolve("crypto-browserify") } }'
  If you don't want to include a polyfill, you can use an empty module option to resole like this:
        _ assign this in Webpack-5 config file: 'resolve: { fallback: { "crypto": false } }'
```

> Hi @svenanderson 👋 Thank you for the PR. Here is a list of changes from my initial review:
> 
>     * The demo has to be removed or users should not be allowed to add more items to the list
> 
>     * The instructions are only for Vercel. Next.js examples are platform agnostic, so if you can add instructions of how to do it without Vercel, please do, then you can mention how it works with Vercel
> 
>     * Update the example to use Function components instead of react classes, as the latter aren't compatible with Fast Refresh
> 
>     * Update the API routes to use es6 (mainly import/export), Next.js takes care of handling the transformation of es6 for Node.js compatibility
> 
>     * Run yarn lint-fix in the Next.js directory and make sure that any lint warnings and errors are handled

@lfades Thanks for your review. I applied the changes that you requested. I also restricted the demo app, so users can not enter features. Can you check them?

Sounds good, thanks! I wasn't entirely sure how to handle this since I found this existing example by chance and didn't know if it should be kept or not.

I'll go ahead and close this PR and create a new one that just has the v2 updates since I also think keeping the v1 example doesn't make too much sense. I definitely want new users to start with v2 and the latest version of Next.js :)

author: Timer

body:
Will this affect the internal app redirect behaviour too @Timer?

Currently with static page generation, when a user clicks a link to a static page (from within the app) the user waits on their current page until the static page is ready, then they are directed to it. (Currently a user only sees the `if (router.isFallback)` state if they visit the page directly, by which i mean not from within the app or when using a standard anchor tag).

Will this still be the case with the `fallback: 'blocking'` as the page is SSR? Or will it send you immediately to the target page and white screen until ready.
author: AshConnolly

body:
> Currently with static page generation, when a user clicks a link to a static page (from within the app) the user waits on their current page until the static page is ready, then they are directed to it

I think there's no change here.

Now with this, we don't need to add `router.isFallback` conditional check. When directly loading the page, Next.js will serve a page always.

* At the very first time, the request will wait until Next.js generates the page
* In all other times, it'll serve the page from the cache.

author: spanicker

body:
> the stylesheet tag is currently next to its corresponding preload -- see the line right above.
> This is working as intended, please don't change the ordering.
> 
> \cc @janicklas-ralph

Stylesheet tag is still next to corresponding preload. It is just moved right below js preloads as stylesheet tags above js preload tags block all js preloading until stylesheets are recieved.

Note that style sheet is still loaded in the head tag, hence any js script tags and elements in the body. This does not change previous behavior nor order of any resource loading/execution, it only unblocks js preloads.

It occurred to me pr description is worded in a way to raise such concern. I have updated pr description.
author: sko-kr

body:
it is important that the CSS is preloaded and ordered ahead of self bundled JS -- for better FCP.
Current ordering is correct: CSS should be preloaded first with max bandwidth, before JS.
"Unblocking js preloads" results in starving CSS on network, we deliberately changed it to current order from what you are doing.

body:
I see that this code was included in `v9.5.2`, but I'm curious how this was not considered a breaking change? This flag seems to change the build output to be something like `routename.html` or `routename/index.html`. Given that it changes the build output structure, should this not have been considered a breaking change? 

Maybe i'm confused here and would be happy to be corrected.
